analysis.research_question_and_background: Infections with respiratory viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 and influenza are significant international public health concerns. While patients with cancer remain the most vulnerable group, they show poor vaccine response in general.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The RESPONSE study is a prospective cohort study focusing on immunocompromised patients with or without hemato-oncological diseases. It aims to analyze the effect of early and late booster vaccination on humoral and cellular responses, with special focus on T cell-induced immune responses.
analysis.methods: Humoral immune responses will be assessed by measuring binding and neutralizing antibodies using standardized assays. Cellular immunity will be evaluated using functional assays such as flow cytometry and FluoroSpot, as well as in-depth analyses using additional exploratory assays as appropriate.
analysis.main_results: This study was initiated following ethics approval and is currently recruiting participants. Enrollment commenced on March 25, 2025, and is ongoing, whereas biosample collection and follow-up visits are nearing completion for most participants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors aim to investigate factors influencing humoral and cellular vaccine-induced immunity in patients with hematological and oncological malignancies, including state of disease, treatment, and demographic factors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study intends to lay a foundation for a structured translational research platform on vaccination to aim for best protection from infection by different respiratory pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: The RESPONSE study is a prospective cohort study designed to investigate vaccine-induced immune responses in immunocompromised patients with or without hemato-oncological diseases. The study focuses on the effects of early and late booster vaccinations on both humoral and cellular immunity, particularly T-cell responses. Humoral responses will be measured through binding and neutralizing antibody assays, while cellular immunity will be assessed using flow cytometry and FluoroSpot. The study is currently recruiting participants and has ongoing enrollment, with biosample collection and follow-up visits nearing completion. The ultimate goal is to establish a platform for translational research on vaccination to improve protection against respiratory pathogens, with a specific focus on influenza and the recently approved respiratory syncytial virus vaccine. The findings may inform future strategies for vaccine development and administration in immunocompromised populations. The study is in the planning phase and has not yet reported results or limitations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has the potential to fill gaps in clinical surveillance for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) burden.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Using 2,662 influent wastewater samples collected from twenty-four treatment plants in four New York counties, RSV concentrations were measured and compared to RSV hospitalizations from September 2022 to July 2024.
analysis.methods: RSV concentrations in wastewater were measured and compared to RSV hospitalizations, with predictive models used to assess variance explained by wastewater levels.
analysis.main_results: RSV concentrations in wastewater correlated well with RSV hospitalizations (ρ between 0.52 and 0.85, P <0.001), lagging hospitalizations for under 10-year-olds by an average of three weeks but serving as a leading indicator for patients over 50 by up to two weeks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Wastewater-based epidemiology of RSV is a reliable surveillance method that could provide early warning for increases in RSV hospitalizations among older populations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Wastewater surveillance can enhance RSV monitoring, particularly for early detection in older adults, improving public health responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's strength is supported by high correlation and predictive power, though limitations include potential generalizability beyond the studied regions and populations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) surveillance by analyzing 2,662 wastewater samples from New York counties and comparing them to hospitalizations (2022-2024). RSV wastewater levels strongly correlated with hospitalizations (ρ=0.52-0.85, P<0.001), lagging pediatric cases by three weeks but leading adult cases by up to two weeks. Wastewater explained 88% of variance in hospitalizations for those over 50, demonstrating its potential as an early warning tool for RSV outbreaks, particularly in older populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial pediatric lower respiratory tract disease, but the host programs that separate directly infected airway cells from exposed bystander cells are still not fully resolved.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We reanalyzed public single-cell RNA sequencing data from RSV-infected human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived respiratory organoids and used viral transcript capture to distinguish mock cells, RSV RNA-negative bystander cells and RSV RNA-positive cells.
analysis.methods: Curated ligand-receptor analysis, exploratory virtual perturbation, multi-layer host-target ranking and drug-signature reversal highlighted IL11, PSAT1, GREM1, PTGS2, SERPINE1, NT5E/CD73 and TNFRSF12A/Fn14 as candidate host nodes.
analysis.main_results: RSV-positive cells made up 12.61% of the atlas and showed viral-load-linked stress, epithelial injury-repair, paracrine remodeling, CD73/adenosine and metabolic programs, not merely stronger interferon responses. Bystander cells, by contrast, were enriched for interferon-stimulated and antiviral sensing states.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings set priorities for experimental follow-up but do not establish functional rescue or therapeutic efficacy. Together, the study defines a focused set of RSV organoid host-response candidates for functional screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: External organoid bulk RNA-seq (GSE263272), antibody-treated organoid scRNA-seq used as a treatment-endpoint reference (GSE263271), primary airway epithelial data (GSE32139) and an in-house RSV time-course qPCR screen supported the injury-remodeling model, while showing that individual candidates vary by context.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In silico perturbation placed NT5E/CD73 among network-relevant secondary-tier nodes and ranked the SYK inhibitor Fostamatinib/R406 highly in drug-signature reversal. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on computational predictions and lack of functional validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated host responses to Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in human airway organoids using single-cell RNA sequencing and viral transcript capture. The researchers distinguished between RSV-infected cells (12.61% of the atlas) and bystander cells, finding that infected cells exhibited viral-load-linked stress, injury-repair, and metabolic programs, while bystander cells showed interferon-stimulated states. Through computational analysis, they identified candidate host nodes including IL11, PSAT1, GREM1, PTGS2, SERPINE1, NT5E/CD73, and TNFRSF12A/Fn14. External datasets supported the injury-remodeling model, though individual candidates varied by context. The study prioritizes these candidates for functional screening but notes that findings do not establish therapeutic efficacy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: To assess the effect of nirsevimab in preventing hospitalizations for lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) during the second respiratory season of life among infants who were administered nirsevimab in their first months of life.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Community-based case-control study conducted in 9 tertiary pediatric hospitals in Andalusia, Southern Spain, including infants born between April 1, 2023, and March 31, 2024, with cases being infants hospitalized for LRTI during the 2024 to 2025 season.
analysis.methods: For each case, 4 community controls were matched by birthdate and province; exposure was nirsevimab administration during the 2023 to 2024 respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) season; the main outcome was hospitalization for LRTI during the 2024 to 2025 season; inverse probability weighting (IPW) and doubly robust augmented IPW (AIPW) models were used to estimate the average treatment effect, expressed as absolute risk reduction (ARR).
analysis.main_results: The study included 1375 infants (275 cases and 1100 controls); nirsevimab administration was associated with a 17.0% ARR (95% CI, 3.2%-30.8%) in LRTI hospitalizations during the 2024 to 2025 season in the AIPW model; stronger associations were observed among RSV-positive cases (ARR = 25.4%; 95% CI, 4.9%-45.8%) and in infants with a history of inhaler use (ARR = 27.7%; 95% CI, 6.4%-48.9%); a negative control exposure (rotavirus vaccination) showed no association, supporting no evidence of relevant residual confounding regarding health-seeking behaviors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Nirsevimab administration was associated with a reduction in second-season LRTI hospitalizations, suggesting meaningful benefits beyond the season of administration and potential implications for future cost-effectiveness evaluations.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the potential extended benefits of nirsevimab in reducing LRTI hospitalizations during the second respiratory season, supporting its use in infant RSV prevention programs and future cost-effectiveness analyses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design is a case-control study, which may introduce selection bias; however, the use of inverse probability weighting and a negative control exposure strengthens the evidence, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This community-based case-control study assessed the effect of nirsevimab in preventing hospitalizations for lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) during the second respiratory season of life. Conducted in 9 tertiary pediatric hospitals in Andalusia, Spain, the study included 1375 infants (275 cases and 1100 controls). Nirsevimab administration during the first RSV season was associated with a 17.0% absolute risk reduction in LRTI hospitalizations during the second season, with stronger effects observed in RSV-positive cases and infants with a history of inhaler use. The use of inverse probability weighting models and a negative control exposure supported the findings, suggesting meaningful benefits beyond the season of administration and implications for future cost-effectiveness evaluations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess whether ward-based surveillance complements community and emergency department (ED) surveillance for respiratory viruses. Respiratory virus circulation may vary across healthcare settings and age groups, potentially limiting the interpretability of surveillance based on a single source.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed molecular test results from respiratory samples collected in community, ED, and hospital ward settings in Milan, Italy, from January 1, 2024, to October 12, 2025. Viruses included influenza A (IAV), influenza B (IBV), RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 (with extended panels in a subset).
analysis.methods: The study integrated data from molecular tests conducted across multiple healthcare settings, including community, ED, and hospital wards, to assess respiratory virus positivity and peak timing.
analysis.main_results: Among 8029 samples, overall positivity for ≥ 1 virus was 46.8%, highest in ED (51.1%) and community (50.5%) and lower in wards (36.7%) (p < 0.001). RSV reappeared first in community (W37/2024) and peaked in community/ED (W50/2024) and later in wards (W2/2025).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that respiratory virus positivity and descriptive peak timing differed across healthcare settings and age groups, highlighting the value of integrated, multi-setting surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that integrated, multi-setting surveillance can improve situational awareness for respiratory viruses, particularly when considering differences in tested populations, testing indications, and clinical outcome availability.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on molecular test results and the potential for differences in testing practices across settings to affect interpretability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed respiratory virus circulation in Milan, Italy, across community, emergency department, and hospital ward settings from January 1, 2024, to October 12, 2025. It found that overall positivity for respiratory viruses was highest in emergency departments and community settings, with lower rates in hospital wards. RSV reappeared first in community settings and peaked later in wards. The authors concluded that integrated, multi-setting surveillance can improve situational awareness when considering differences in tested populations and testing practices. The study's findings highlight the importance of combining data from various healthcare settings to better understand respiratory virus epidemiology. However, the study is observational and may be limited by variations in testing protocols and population characteristics, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on invasive group A streptococcal infections (iGAS) in children, examining their early recognition, diagnostic approach, and emergency department management in the post-COVID era. The central question is how to improve outcomes through heightened clinical vigilance and rapid intervention.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that synthesizes current epidemiological studies, clinical evidence, and guideline recommendations on pediatric iGAS. It emphasizes early warning signs, diagnostic strategies, and time-critical emergency department management.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus on the post-pandemic resurgence of pediatric iGAS with increased severity and higher ICU admission rates. Key conclusions include the importance of early recognition of red flags, rapid diagnostic evaluation, and prompt initiation of appropriate management to reduce morbidity and mortality.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not explicitly mention controversies or specific evidence gaps, but it highlights the need for heightened clinical vigilance due to the resurgence of cases and increased severity.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Implications include the need for early recognition of warning signs, rapid sepsis resuscitation, early combination antibiotic therapy, urgent surgical consultation for suspected necrotizing infections, and consideration of adjunctive therapies like intravenous immunoglobulin in toxin-mediated disease.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review addresses the resurgence of pediatric invasive group A streptococcal infections (iGAS) in the post-COVID era, emphasizing their life-threatening nature and increased severity. It synthesizes current epidemiological data, clinical evidence, and guidelines to provide practical guidance for emergency physicians. Key findings include a marked rise in iGAS incidence since 2022, with risk factors such as age under five, viral respiratory coinfections, and virulent emm serotypes. The review stresses the importance of early recognition of warning signs, rapid diagnostic evaluation, and prompt management, including antibiotic therapy and surgical consultation, to reduce morbidity and mortality.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute bronchiolitis is a common and clinically heterogeneous lower respiratory tract infection in infancy, and while current guidelines discourage routine bronchodilator use, physiological responsiveness may exist in some patients. Tidal breathing analysis (TBA) offers a non-invasive, bedside method to objectively assess respiratory mechanics and quantify physiological changes after bronchodilator administration.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case study reports on a 23-month-old boy with severe RSV bronchiolitis-like wheezing illness complicated by acute respiratory failure, in whom bronchodilator responsiveness was evaluated using predefined TBA parameters before and after inhaled bronchodilator administration.
analysis.methods: Bronchodilator responsiveness was assessed using tidal breathing analysis (TBA) to measure predefined parameters including time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF), tPTEF/TE ratio, expiratory time (TE), total respiratory cycle duration (Ttot), tidal volume (VT), minute ventilation (MV), and peak expiratory flow before and after bronchodilator administration.
analysis.main_results: Following treatment, tPTEF increased from 0.17 to 0.33 s (+94%), and the tPTEF/TE ratio increased from 0.12 to 0.27 (+125%). TE and Ttot decreased by 12.6% and 5.1%, respectively, while VT and MV increased by 12.1% and 18.3%. Peak expiratory flow remained unchanged at 0.14 L/s.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This is among the first reports using bedside TBA to characterize acute bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness, with improvements in expiratory timing indices consistent with improved expiratory flow dynamics, supporting the hypothesis of a bronchodilator-responsive physiological phenotype.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that TBA-defined bronchodilator responsiveness may represent an early physiological marker in severe bronchiolitis, potentially supporting individualized treatment strategies and informing future longitudinal studies on its predictive value for recurrent wheezing or asthma.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This is a single case study, limiting generalizability and statistical power, but the objective measurements and clear physiological changes provide moderate evidence for the feasibility of TBA in assessing bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis.

analysis.summary_en: This case study investigates tidal breathing analysis (TBA) as a non-invasive method to assess bronchodilator responsiveness in a 23-month-old boy with severe RSV bronchiolitis complicated by respiratory failure. Using TBA parameters, the study objectively measured significant improvements in expiratory timing indices (tPTEF increased by 94%, tPTEF/TE ratio by 125%) and ventilation parameters after bronchodilator administration, while peak expiratory flow remained unchanged. The findings demonstrate the feasibility of bedside TBA in identifying physiological bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis, suggesting a potential bronchodilator-responsive phenotype. This approach may support individualized treatment strategies and warrants prospective longitudinal studies to validate TBA-defined responsiveness as an early physiological marker for predicting outcomes like recurrent wheezing or asthma.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) with a considerable disease burden among children under 5 years of age.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of RSV, genetic diversity of circulating strains, and amino acid variability in viral proteins, as well as identify mutations within the binding sites of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) approved for RSV prophylaxis.
analysis.methods: Nasopharyngeal specimens from 5,170 patients of all ages with ARI were tested for 13 respiratory viruses using multiplex real-time PCR. Representative RSV-positive samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, followed by phylogenetic and amino acid sequence analyses.
analysis.main_results: RSV was positive in 303 (5.9%) patients, of whom 61 (20.1%) had co-infections with other respiratory viruses. Among children under 5 years of age, RSV was the most frequently detected pathogen in cases of bronchiolitis (30.6%) and pneumonia (12.6%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The absence of resistance-associated substitutions in the F protein indicates that currently circulating RSV strains remain susceptible to approved mAbs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide important insights into the genetic diversity of RSV strains and their susceptibility to monoclonal antibodies, which can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and the development of targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to data from the 2024-2025 season and does not account for long-term trends or seasonal variations. The evidence is strong as it is based on direct testing and sequencing of RSV-positive samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and genetic diversity of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Bulgaria from 2023 to 2025. RSV was detected in 5.9% of patients with acute respiratory infections (ARIs), with a notable proportion of co-infections. Among children under 5, RSV was the most frequently identified pathogen in bronchiolitis and pneumonia cases. Whole-genome sequencing revealed substantial genetic diversity, with eight and seven lineages identified in RSV-A and RSV-B, respectively. The most prevalent lineages were A.D.1.11 and B.D.1.1. No resistance-associated substitutions were found in the F protein antigenic sites of RSV-A, suggesting susceptibility to approved monoclonal antibodies. In contrast, RSV-B strains showed substitutions in multiple antigenic sites. The study highlights the importance of monitoring RSV genetic variation for effective surveillance and treatment strategies. The evidence is strong, but the findings are limited to a single season, reducing generalizability.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize the whole genome of RSV strains circulating in two Italian areas during the 2024-2025 RSV season, the first after implementation of the national nirsevimab prophylaxis program, due to limited investigation of genetic variation at inter- and intra-host levels.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Whole genome sequencing was performed on 88 respiratory samples that tested positive for RSV from patients who had not received nirsevimab prophylaxis.
analysis.methods: A newly designed bioinformatic pipeline was developed to evaluate genetic variation within hosts and reveal minority mutation distribution among RSV lineages, with phylogenetic inference to correlate strains with European circulation.
analysis.main_results: RSV-A (n=54) showed significantly higher nucleotide diversity than RSV-B (n=34), with A.D.3 being the most prevalent RSV-A lineage (64%), while all RSV-B strains were B.D.E.; the G, L and F genes showed the highest variability, and no mutations known to reduce nirsevimab efficacy were detected.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The elevated diversity in RSV-A resulted from a wider distribution of mutations across the genome, including both high-frequency and low-frequency variants, highlighting the importance of continued genomic surveillance to detect potential escape variants as prophylactic programs expand.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance strategies for RSV evolution under nirsevimab implementation, emphasizing the need to monitor minority variants that could impact prophylaxis efficacy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The absence of nirsevimab-treated patients limits direct assessment of escape variants, but the study provides high-confidence evidence on RSV genomic diversity and minority variant dynamics due to robust sequencing and bioinformatic analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized the genomic evolution and minority variant dynamics of RSV during the first season of nirsevimab implementation in Italy (2024-2025). Whole genome sequencing of 88 RSV-positive samples revealed significantly higher nucleotide diversity in RSV-A compared to RSV-B, with A.D.3 being the predominant RSV-A lineage. The G, L, and F genes showed the highest variability, and no mutations known to reduce nirsevimab efficacy were detected. The findings highlight the importance of continued genomic surveillance to monitor potential escape variants as prophylactic programs expand, providing critical insights for public health strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the clinical course of viral respiratory infections, specifically focusing on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), in hospitalized adults during the 2025/2026 season in Poland, as contemporary comparative data are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective multicenter study was conducted on consecutive adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV, influenza, or COVID-19 infections between September 2025 and April 2026. Most hospitalized patients were elderly and unvaccinated.
analysis.methods: Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, vaccination status, clinical features, laboratory findings, and outcomes were analyzed. Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: The study included 604 patients: 255 with COVID-19, 314 with influenza, and 35 with RSV infection. RSV patients were older, more frequently affected by multimorbidity, ischemic heart disease, and cancer, and showed the greatest respiratory impairment, including the highest rates of hypoxemia and pneumonia.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the distinct clinical profiles of RSV compared to other respiratory viruses, emphasizing its impact on respiratory impairment and comorbidities in older adults.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results underscore the importance of targeted surveillance, improved vaccination strategies for older adults, and enhanced hospital preparedness for RSV-related respiratory morbidity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the data provide a moderate assessment of RSV's clinical impact in hospitalized adults.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared the clinical course of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and other respiratory viruses in hospitalized adults during the 2025/2026 season in Poland. It found that RSV patients were older, had more comorbidities, and exhibited greater respiratory impairment, including higher rates of hypoxemia and pneumonia, compared to those with influenza or COVID-19. The study supports the need for improved vaccination strategies, continued surveillance, and hospital preparedness for RSV. However, the retrospective nature of the study and abstract-only evidence limit the confidence in the findings, which are considered to have moderate strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) accounts for 33 million infections worldwide each year and is the leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants. The RSV small hydrophobic (SH) protein has been previously implicated in regulating the secretion of IL-1β following infection, but its role in modulating RSV disease severity beyond IL-1β production remains unknown.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized a recombinant A2 laboratory strain virus encoded with an aspartic acid at amino acid 63 (A2 SH N63D) to investigate the impact of the N64 mutation. Experiments were conducted in mice and human monocyte THP-1 cell lines with a dual reporter for NF-κB and type I IFN response.
analysis.methods: Plaque assays, ELISAs, qPCR for cytosolic mtDNA, and human monocyte THP-1 cell lines with a dual reporter for NF-κB and type I IFN response were used to study the impact of the N64 mutation. The A2 SH N63D mutant was generated and compared to the wildtype A2 (WT A2).
analysis.main_results: The A2 SH N63D mutant elicited decreased viral titers and early disease compared to the wildtype A2 in mice. Increased inflammatory cytokines and a type I IFN response were observed following A2 SH N63D infection, along with mtDNA release within THP-1 cells and a STING-dependent type I IFN response.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest that the aspartic acid within the C-terminus of the SH protein may contribute to RSV pathogenesis and the type I IFN response. This finding is novel as it expands the understanding of the SH protein's role beyond IL-1β modulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of targeted therapies against RSV by focusing on the SH protein's role in pathogenesis. Understanding the SH protein's impact on disease severity could lead to improved surveillance and intervention strategies for RSV infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in mice and THP-1 cell lines, which may not fully recapitulate human RSV infection. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of the study and the use of laboratory strains rather than clinical isolates.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the RSV small hydrophobic (SH) protein in viral pathogenesis, focusing on a specific mutation (N64D) observed in a 2017 outbreak. The researchers generated a recombinant A2 SH N63D mutant and compared it to wildtype A2 in mice and THP-1 cells. The mutant showed decreased viral titers and early disease in mice, along with increased inflammatory cytokines and a type I IFN response. The findings suggest that the aspartic acid in the SH protein's C-terminus contributes to RSV pathogenesis and the type I IFN response, potentially informing targeted therapies and surveillance strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The immunogenicity of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination in immunocompromised individuals is poorly understood due to limited published data in this population, specifically on cellular responses to novel RSV vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In a national prospective observational cohort, 44 immunocompromised individuals reported receiving either adjuvanted RSVPreF3 (AREXVYTM) or unadjuvanted RSVpreF (ABRYSVOTM). The cohort was predominantly solid organ transplant recipients but also included participants with autoimmune conditions on immunosuppressants.
analysis.methods: T-cell responses, RSV preF antibodies, and RSV neutralizing antibodies were assessed at baseline, early (2 or 4 weeks), and late (12 weeks) post-vaccination using flow cytometry following RSV-A2 fusion protein peptide pool stimulation, ELISA, and live-virus neutralization, respectively.
analysis.main_results: Post-vaccination, there were significant increases in RSV-specific memory CD4+ T-cells producing IFN-γ, IL-2, and TNF, and increases in polyfunctional CD4+ T-cells. Both vaccines, without significant differences, increased CD4+ T-cell polyfunctionality.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that sustained T-cell metabolic fitness, as indicated by GLUT1, may be linked to the durability of both cellular and humoral immune responses. Understanding the role of GLUT1 in shaping immune responses may provide novel methods for optimizing vaccine strategies for immunocompromised individuals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies GLUT1 as a potential biomarker for predicting sustained antibody responses and polyfunctional T-cell responses post-RSV vaccination in immunocompromised individuals, which could inform personalized vaccine strategies and improve outcomes in this vulnerable population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was observational and included a small sample size of 44 immunocompromised individuals, which may limit generalizability. However, the use of multiple assays and longitudinal assessments provides moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunogenicity of RSV vaccination in immunocompromised individuals, focusing on T-cell responses and their correlation with antibody durability. In a cohort of 44 immunocompromised participants, both adjuvanted and unadjuvanted RSV vaccines significantly increased polyfunctional CD4+ T-cells and cytokine production. GLUT1 expression in memory CD4+ T-cells correlated with sustained antibody titers and polyfunctionality at 12 weeks post-vaccination, suggesting a role for T-cell metabolic fitness in durable immunity. The findings highlight GLUT1 as a potential biomarker for vaccine response and could guide optimized vaccination strategies for immunocompromised individuals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors targeting the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) L-RdRp complex, a promising but underexploited drug target, due to the limitations of current virtual screening strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This computational study employed a multi-dimensional computer-aided drug screening framework integrating activity, toxicity, drug-likeness, and stability to identify potential RSV L-RdRp inhibitors.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed two OECD-compliant 2D-QSAR models to predict inhibitory activity and cytotoxicity, followed by a four-step screening workflow including QSAR-based filtering, molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, and molecular dynamics simulations.
analysis.main_results: The optimal inhibitory activity model showed strong statistical performance (R2 = 0.8281, QLOO2 = 0.7653, Rtest2 = 0.8713), while the cytotoxicity model achieved R2 = 0.8263, Rtest2 = 0.8951; ultimately, five candidate compounds were selected with predicted higher activity and lower cytotoxicity than remdesivir.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as providing valuable in silico-derived lead candidates and a reliable computational workflow for identifying experimental L-RdRp inhibitors targeting RSV, representing a novel approach to drug discovery for this virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These computational results could inform the development of more effective and safer RSV therapeutics, potentially improving treatment options for RSV infections, which remain a significant public health burden.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate as this study relied entirely on computational predictions without experimental validation, though the rigorous validation of QSAR models and comprehensive screening workflow support the reliability of the in silico findings.

analysis.summary_en: This computational study identified five promising small-molecule inhibitors targeting the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) L-RdRp complex through a multi-dimensional screening framework. The researchers developed rigorously validated 2D-QSAR models to predict inhibitory activity and cytotoxicity, followed by molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, and molecular dynamics simulations. All five selected candidates demonstrated predicted higher inhibitory activity, lower cytotoxicity, stable binding modes, and favorable oral bioavailability compared to remdesivir. While these in silico results provide valuable lead candidates and a reliable computational workflow for RSV drug discovery, experimental validation is needed to confirm their efficacy and safety.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory viruses cause significant morbidity and mortality in very young and old, but the mechanisms of mortality are unknown. This study investigated the effect of Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) on maintaining airway epithelium polarity during RSV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used human bronchial epithelial cells (hBEC) grown in transwell pretreated with NRG1 before RSV infection. Cells were treated with anti-ERBb2 and anti-ERBb3 antibodies, and immunohistochemistry was performed for polarity markers.
analysis.methods: hBEC were pretreated with human NRG1 (100 ng) for 5 days before RSV-gfp infection. Immunohistochemistry was performed for CRB3 and DLG1 markers, and mitochondrial superoxide production was detected using MitoSOX indicators.
analysis.main_results: NRG1 prevented disruption of CRB3 localization by RSV, an effect blocked by anti-ERBb3. NRG1 treatment also reduced mitoROS in RSV-infected cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that NRG1 stabilizes airway epithelium by preventing disruption of apico-basal polarity and reducing excessive ROS during RSV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest NRG1 could be a therapeutic candidate to protect airway epithelial integrity during RSV infection, potentially reducing disease severity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro using hBEC, limiting generalizability to in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the controlled laboratory setting but supported by specific mechanistic findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) as a protective agent against RSV-induced disruption of human airway epithelium polarity. Using human bronchial epithelial cells pretreated with NRG1 before RSV infection, the researchers found that NRG1 prevented disruption of CRB3 localization, an effect blocked by anti-ERBb3 antibodies. NRG1 also reduced mitochondrial ROS production in infected cells. The study demonstrates that NRG1 stabilizes airway epithelium by maintaining polarity and reducing oxidative stress during RSV infection, suggesting potential therapeutic applications.

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review examines the role of blood eosinophils (BEO) in managing acute paediatric wheeze, focusing on their measurement and clinical utility during exacerbations in children under 16 years.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A scoping review following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching Medline, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science for studies published in the last 20 years. Eight heterogeneous studies (n = 855) were included, comprising five observational/retrospective studies and three randomised controlled trials.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: BEO reporting varied widely with inconsistent units, cut-offs and poorly described sampling timing. No study used point-of-care testing. Eosinophil dynamics differed by age, wheeze phenotype, disease severity and viral aetiology, preventing meaningful comparison. Evidence supporting eosinophil-guided corticosteroid use was limited.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is a paucity of high-quality data describing BEO during acute wheeze exacerbations in children. Current evidence is largely derived from stable outpatient cohorts and may not be directly applicable to acute settings. Heterogeneity in study design and reporting limits comparability.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective studies with standardised sampling of BEO during acute presentations are needed to inform precision-based corticosteroid use. Two studies suggested improved outcomes with systemic corticosteroids in children with rhinovirus-associated wheeze and higher BEO, while lower BEO were observed in RSV-associated wheeze.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review maps the evidence on blood eosinophils (BEO) in acute paediatric wheeze management. Eight heterogeneous studies showed inconsistent BEO reporting, with no point-of-care testing used. Eosinophil dynamics varied by age, phenotype, severity and viral aetiology, limiting comparability. Evidence for eosinophil-guided corticosteroids was limited, though two studies suggested benefits in rhinovirus-associated wheeze with higher BEO. High-quality data from acute settings is lacking, with most evidence from stable cohorts. Standardised prospective sampling is needed to guide precision corticosteroid use.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a pathogen that infects nearly all children by age two, causing severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, particularly premature babies and those with comorbidities. The central question addresses inequities in infant RSV immunization access in low- and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This dissertation uses five research types across the translational spectrum: public health, basic, preclinical, clinical, and implementation research. It includes a review of the RSV vaccine/mAb landscape (5 marketed products, 30 in development as of June 2024), co-creation workshops with healthcare workers in Soweto, South Africa, development and validation of a dried blood RSV-neutralizing antibody assay, and industry-independent development of intranasal palivizumab drops.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Nirsevimab shows >80% effectiveness against RSV hospitalization, but access remains concentrated in high-income countries despite LMICs bearing the greatest disease burden. The dried blood assay (R2 > 0.95) successfully replaced serum in bioanalyses and was transferred to a Ghanaian laboratory. Intranasal palivizumab was safe but did not significantly prevent RSV infection in a phase 2b RCT. RSM01 has a higher resistance barrier against mutants, and resistance generally reduces viral fitness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: LMIC implementation of RSV prevention lags due to logistical and financial barriers and gaps in safety and efficacy data. Intranasal mAbs showed no reduction in viral titer despite reducing symptomatic infections, suggesting they are unlikely to be a viable, cost-effective protection strategy. Current RSV product development follows a "trickle-down" approach designed for high-income contexts.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: An equity-by-design framework is proposed with four recommendations: scientific co-ownership with LMIC partners, operational investment in local capacity, economic feasibility built in from early development, and social integration with community priorities. Access-to-medicine mechanisms (voluntary licensing, technology transfer) combined with WHO prequalification and funding mechanisms like Gavi are essential for affordable LMIC access.

analysis.summary_en: This dissertation addresses inequities in infant RSV immunization access in LMICs through five research types. It finds nirsevimab is highly effective but access remains inequitable, while intranasal mAbs show limited promise. The dried blood assay successfully transferred to Ghana, building local capacity. The thesis proposes an equity-by-design framework with recommendations for co-ownership, local investment, early affordability, and community integration, positioning equity as foundational rather than an afterthought in RSV immunization development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory viruses, such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza A (H1N1), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), remain major public health threats due to overlapping clinical symptoms and the limited speed, sensitivity, and multiplexing capacity of conventional diagnostic methods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study presents a label-free optical biosensing platform based on subwavelength grating microring resonators (SGMRRs) for the sensitive and specific detection of viral antigens.
analysis.methods: The sensor surface is functionalized with antibodies against three representative viral proteins, enabling quantitative detection via resonance wavelength shifts upon antigen binding.
analysis.main_results: The platform achieves a refractive index limit of detection (LoD) of 1.25×10−4 RIU and enables the detection of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein at 100 pg/mL, the H1N1 nucleoprotein at 10 pg/mL, and the RSV F-trimer protein at 10 pg/mL.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The compact SGMRR design readily supports multiplexed integration through multi-ring or multi-channel architectures, highlighting its potential as a scalable and high-performance platform for rapid, quantitative, and point-of-care viral diagnostics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This technology offers a promising solution for improving the detection of respiratory viruses, including RSV, with high sensitivity and multiplexing capabilities, which could enhance diagnostic accuracy and speed in clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on an abstract-only report, which may lack detailed validation and real-world testing; however, the reported performance metrics suggest strong evidence for the platform's potential.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a label-free optical biosensing platform using subwavelength grating microring resonators (SGMRRs) for sensitive detection of respiratory viruses, including RSV. The sensor, functionalized with antibodies against viral proteins, achieves a low limit of detection (1.25×10−4 RIU) and detects RSV F-trimer protein at 10 pg/mL. The compact design supports multiplexing, offering a scalable solution for rapid, point-of-care diagnostics. While the abstract reports promising performance, further validation is needed to confirm real-world applicability.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the immune dysregulation in Down syndrome that increases susceptibility to infections and affects vaccine response, particularly focusing on respiratory syncytial virus.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of cohort studies in both pediatric and adult populations with Down syndrome, examining immune alterations and their association with severe respiratory viral infections and reduced vaccine-induced immunity.
analysis.methods: The methods involved integrating molecular, cellular, and clinical evidence from existing cohort studies to define the interferon-driven immune phenotype in Down syndrome and its implications for susceptibility to infection and vaccination response.
analysis.main_results: Cohort studies reported higher rates of hospitalization and mortality, along with lower peak antibody titers and more rapid waning of immunity following vaccination in individuals with Down syndrome.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence of a distinct immune phenotype in Down syndrome that is driven by interferon hyperactivation, which has implications for understanding the mechanisms behind increased susceptibility to respiratory viral infections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a framework for developing tailored preventive strategies and optimizing vaccination approaches in individuals with Down syndrome to address their heightened risk of severe respiratory viral infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing cohort data and does not present new experimental results, which limits the depth of mechanistic understanding. However, the integration of multiple lines of evidence supports a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores immune dysregulation in Down syndrome, highlighting its role in increased susceptibility to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections and altered vaccine responses. The study integrates molecular, cellular, and clinical evidence from existing cohort studies, revealing that individuals with Down syndrome experience higher hospitalization and mortality rates, along with reduced vaccine-induced immunity. These findings suggest a distinct interferon-driven immune phenotype that may inform targeted preventive strategies and vaccination optimization. The study's reliance on existing data limits its depth of mechanistic insight, though the synthesis of multiple evidence sources provides a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe acute respiratory infections (SARIs) impose substantial paediatric morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, and contemporary aetiological data are needed to guide prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cross-sectional analytic study was conducted among Kenyan children aged 0–18 years hospitalised with SARI and a positive nasopharyngeal swab multiplex qRT-PCR test between March 2018 and March 2023.
analysis.methods: Multiplex quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) tests, BioFire® respiratory panel 2.0 (RP 2) and 2.1 plus (RP2.1 plus), were used to detect pathogens; cases were analyzed for clinical characteristics, radiological features, laboratory data, seasonality and risk factors for severe infection.
analysis.main_results: A total of 545 pathogens were detected in 382 cases, with 123 (22.5%) polymicrobial detections, 14 (4%) severe illnesses and three (0.8%) deaths; rhinovirus (24%) and respiratory syncytial virus (21%) were the most common viral pathogens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Viruses accounted for the majority of respiratory infections, and infections peaked during the first dry season and the short rainy season, suggesting seasonality-driven scheduling of respiratory vaccines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings indicate that RSV contributes substantially to paediatric SARI hospitalisations in Kenya and that vaccine timing should align with seasonal peaks to maximise impact.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design and reliance on multiplex PCR without confirmatory viral culture limit causal inference and may underestimate co-infections, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cross-sectional study in Kenyan children hospitalised with SARI used multiplex qRT-PCR to identify respiratory pathogens between 2018 and 2023. Among 382 cases, 545 pathogens were detected, with RSV identified in 21% of infections, second only to rhinovirus. Viral aetiology predominated, and infections peaked during the first dry season and short rainy season. Lower respiratory tract involvement and comorbidities such as asthma and vitamin D deficiency were associated with severe disease. The authors conclude that RSV is a major contributor to paediatric SARI and recommend aligning vaccination schedules with seasonal peaks to reduce burden.

analysis.research_question_and_background: To construct a nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP), so as to provide evidence for clinical intervention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data of 569 infants with MPP hospitalized in the Department of Respiratory Medicine and Department of Infectious Diseases, Children’s Hospital of Soochow University. They were divided into a wheezing group (204 cases) and a non-wheezing group (365 cases) according to symptoms.
analysis.methods: Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used for preliminary screening, followed by Logistic regression to identify independent risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. A nomogram prediction model was established, and its performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and decision curve analysis (DCA).
analysis.main_results: Multivariate Logistic regression showed that history of wheezing (OR = 5.894, 95%CI: 3.541–9.812), history of eczema (OR = 1.951, 95%CI: 1.295–2.939), elevated IgG (OR = 1.166, 95%CI: 1.074–1.266), elevated CKMB (OR = 1.083, 95%CI: 1.007–1.164), and combined HRSV infection (OR = 3.430, 95%CI: 1.819–6.468) were risk factors, while fever (OR = 0.389, 95%CI: 0.252–0.599) was a protective factor against wheezing in infants with MPP.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Atopic constitution and mixed viral infection are risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. The nomogram model is clinically valuable for predicting wheezing in infants with MPP.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The nomogram model can provide evidence for clinical intervention by predicting wheezing in infants with MPP, potentially guiding early identification and management of high-risk patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Although the corrected AUC remained above 0.70, the decline from the training-set AUC (0.786) suggests some degree of overfitting, likely attributable to the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a nomogram to predict wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) using data from 569 hospitalized infants. Multivariate analysis identified history of wheezing, history of eczema, elevated IgG, elevated CKMB, and combined HRSV infection as risk factors, while fever was protective. The nomogram showed moderate discriminative ability (corrected AUC = 0.705) with potential clinical utility. The findings highlight the importance of atopic constitution and mixed viral infections in wheezing risk, though the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size may limit generalizability.

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-28; Study period: November 2019 to August 2025.
analysis.location_and_population: United States; 1,223 healthy children from birth to age 5 years followed at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center.
analysis.event: Confirmed study findings on respiratory virus infections in young children, including RSV, influenza, hMPV, and SARS-CoV-2, highlighting asymptomatic and severe illness patterns.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 15,898 acute respiratory infections identified; 78.4% managed at home, 21.6% in healthcare settings; Infants <1 year had highest asymptomatic rates (14.5% flu, 12.5% RSV) and severe illness risk (OR 2.22-4.73 for RSV/influenza).

analysis.brief_en: A comprehensive study published in Pediatrics analyzed respiratory virus infections in 1,223 U.S. children from 2019-2025, identifying 15,898 infections. Infants showed the highest rates of both asymptomatic infections (up to 14.5% for flu) and severe illness requiring hospital care (OR 2.22-4.73 for RSV/influenza). While 78.4% of cases were managed at home, the findings underscore the vulnerability of infants and suggest infection prevention should include environmental cleaning beyond hand hygiene. The research provides critical insights for pediatric care and public health strategies.
analysis.summary_en: A comprehensive study published in Pediatrics analyzed respiratory virus infections in 1,223 U.S. children from 2019-2025, identifying 15,898 infections. Infants showed the highest rates of both asymptomatic infections (up to 14.5% for flu) and severe illness requiring hospital care (OR 2.22-4.73 for RSV/influenza). While 78.4% of cases were managed at home, the findings underscore the vulnerability of infants and suggest infection prevention should include environmental cleaning beyond hand hygiene. The research provides critical insights for pediatric care and public health strategies.

analysis.time: Published on 24 July 2026. RSV activity is rising toward high levels, typically peaking in winter months from May to October.
analysis.location_and_population: New Zealand, with high rates of serious illness. analysis.event: An explainer article about RSV (respiratory syncytial virus) causing significant winter illness in New Zealand. Health experts are calling for a national childhood vaccination program, citing high hospitalization rates and the availability of vaccines in other countries.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Approximately 1,800-2,000 children are hospitalized annually with RSV, half of whom are infants. analysis.brief_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is causing significant winter illness in New Zealand, with high hospitalization rates among children and older adults. The virus, which spreads through airborne droplets, affects 1,800-2,000 children annually, with infants and those under 1 being particularly vulnerable. Māori and Pasifika children face disproportionately higher risks. While RSV typically causes cold-like symptoms in healthy individuals, it can lead to severe complications like pneumonia and bronchiolitis, especially in immunocompromised individuals. Health experts are advocating for the approval of RSV vaccines already available in other countries, citing evidence of their effectiveness in reducing hospitalizations. Currently, no universal childhood vaccine exists in New Zealand, and treatment remains supportive care.

analysis.time: The study was conducted between November 30, 2021, and November 20, 2025, with results published online July 20, 2026, and accessed July 23, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The phase 3 randomized trial was conducted across 110 sites in 27 countries and territories, involving 1003 infants at increased risk of severe RSV disease, including those with chronic lung disease and congenital heart disease.
analysis.event: Clesrovimab demonstrated safety and tolerability through a second RSV season in high-risk infants, with a 210-mg dose showing comparable adverse event profiles to palivizumab in the first season.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In RSV season 1, 498 infants received 105 mg of clesrovimab and 499 received palivizumab; in season 2, 276 infants received 210 mg of clesrovimab. Adverse events were comparable between groups (75.3% vs 79.6% in season 1; 66.7% vs 68.1% in season 2), with most being grade 1 or 2.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study confirmed clesrovimab's safety through two RSV seasons but was limited by the absence of a comparator arm in season 2 and a smaller sample size for noninferiority assessment. The single-dose regimen was noted as potentially improving adherence in this vulnerable population.

analysis.brief_en: A recent phase 3 study published in JAMA Pediatrics demonstrates that clesrovimab (Enflonsia; Merck) remains well tolerated through a second RSV season in high-risk infants. Conducted across 110 sites in 27 countries, the trial involved 1003 infants, with 276 receiving a 210-mg dose in the second season. Adverse events were comparable between clesrovimab and palivizumab groups (75.3% vs 79.6% in season 1; 66.7% vs 68.1% in season 2), with most being mild to moderate. The study supports clesrovimab's safety as a single-dose RSV prevention, though limitations included no comparator in season 2 and reduced statistical power. The findings highlight the potential for improved adherence with a single-dose regimen in this vulnerable population.

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-26. The study evaluated data across two RSV seasons, with the first season's analysis through day 150 and the second season's through day 180.
analysis.location_and_population: Conducted across 27 countries and territories with 997 high-risk infants enrolled from 110 sites. Participants were infants at increased risk of severe RSV disease, including those born prematurely or with chronic lung disease or congenital heart disease.
analysis.event: A phase 3 randomized clinical trial (SMART trial) published in JAMA Pediatrics found that clesrovimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody, was well tolerated for RSV prevention through two RSV seasons in high-risk infants. The study compared a single dose of clesrovimab with monthly palivizumab during the first season and assessed a higher 210-mg dose in the second season.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among 997 infants, adverse event rates were comparable between clesrovimab and palivizumab groups during the first season. The incidence of RSV-associated medically attended lower respiratory infection (MALRI) was similar (3.2% vs 3.4%). In the second season, the cumulative incidence of RSV-associated MALRI with the 210-mg dose was 7.3%. The study did not establish noninferiority versus palivizumab due to limited power.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The trial confirmed clesrovimab's safety and tolerability across two seasons but noted limitations, including the absence of a comparator group in the second season, unadjusted safety comparisons, and lack of long-term respiratory outcome data. The authors concluded that the single-dose regimen may simplify prevention and improve adherence compared to monthly injections.

analysis.brief_en: A JAMA Pediatrics study confirms that clesrovimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody, is well tolerated for RSV prevention in high-risk infants across two RSV seasons. The phase 3 SMART trial enrolled 997 infants across 27 countries, comparing a single clesrovimab dose to monthly palivizumab in the first season and a higher 210-mg dose in the second. Adverse event rates were comparable, and RSV infection rates were similar between groups. While the single-dose regimen offers potential adherence benefits, limitations included no second-season comparator and insufficient power to prove noninferiority. The findings support clesrovimab's extended use in infants at continued risk.

analysis.brief_en: A July 24, 2026 Popular Science article examines disease transmission risks on cruise ships, specifically addressing respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) alongside other illnesses. The article, featuring insights from infectious disease experts Dr. William Schaffner and Dr. Freedman, clarifies that while cruise ships do pose higher transmission risks due to prolonged close contact, RSV and other respiratory infections are generally mild for most passengers. While acknowledging increased risks for older travelers and those with compromised immune systems, the article emphasizes that cruise lines have implemented effective prevention measures, evidenced by a 50% reduction in gastrointestinal illness rates over recent years. The article also contextualizes recent hantavirus outbreaks as anomalies rather than typical cruise ship risks.

analysis.time: Survey conducted July 1-5, 2026; findings released July 22, 2026; article published July 24, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: United States; nationally representative sample of 1,031 US adults.
analysis.event: A survey by the Annenberg Public Policy Center revealed that most Americans are unaware or unsure of CDC's recommended vaccines during pregnancy, including flu, Tdap, RSV, hepatitis B, and COVID-19 vaccines.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Awareness ranged from 23% (hepatitis B) to 48% (flu vaccine); 45-66% of adults were unsure about recommendations; women aged 18-49 were more knowledgeable but still uncertain; pharmacists identified as key providers needing to address knowledge gaps.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC guidance exists but is not widely known; ACOG has issued separate recommendations including COVID-19; pharmacists face challenges reconciling potentially conflicting guidance sources; survey methodology included web and telephone sampling with a 53.5% completion rate.

analysis.brief_en: A recent survey by the Annenberg Public Policy Center reveals significant public unawareness of CDC's recommended vaccines during pregnancy. Conducted July 1-5, 2026, among 1,031 US adults, the study found that awareness of recommended vaccines (flu, Tdap, RSV, hepatitis B) ranged from just 23% to 48%, with uncertainty being the most common response across all vaccines. Women of childbearing age showed slightly higher awareness but remained largely uninformed. The findings highlight a critical knowledge gap that pharmacists, as key vaccination providers, must address. The survey comes amid policy changes, including a revised ACIP charter and separate maternal immunization recommendations from ACOG, potentially creating confusion for healthcare providers and patients.

analysis.brief_en: New Zealand has reached a significant milestone in the fight against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) with Medsafe approving nirsevimab, a preventive medicine for babies and young children. With Medsafe clearance secured, the focus shifts to Pharmac to ensure timely access before the next RSV season begins.

ae0ac6c71ff738989174236ee83b02c15cea5095.text: 成人 呼吸道合胞病毒 感染和社区获得性肺炎:发病机制、诊断挑战和临床意义。

c03347e9943d9b0eb7d9524e8769d0915be5b484.text: 简介:社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 仍然是成人发病和 死亡率 的重要原因。呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 对成人 CAP 具有重要意义,特别是在老年人和患有慢性心肺疾病的患者中,但由于临床特征与其他呼吸道感染重叠且常规检测有限,因此经常被诊断不足。涵盖领域:本综述总结了 RSV 的关键病毒学和免疫学特征,强调了成人的诊断挑战,并讨论了呼吸道疾病以外的临床后果,包括心血管并发症、严重的院内结局以及抗生素暴露引起的继发细菌感染。利用韩国和国际数据,我们强调多样本分子检测在改善检测方面的价值,并讨论了 CAP 管理中抗菌药物管理的影响。我们还概述了 疫苗 在 3 期试验中的疗效以及在老年人中的早期现实世界疗效。专家意见:减少成人 RSV 负担需要在 RSV 循环期间建立可行的诊断途径,加强 监测 以捕获有临床意义的结果,并针对高危人群进行 疫苗接种。需要对免疫功能低下和其他高危人群进行持续的授权后评估和研究,以优化 疫苗接种 策略并为下一代预防提供信息。

f095d1326c80787c250d70f3f5e37b0db3d0f1c9.text: 该综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染作为成人社区获得性肺炎 (CAP) 的原因,检查其 呼吸道合胞病毒、诊断挑战和临床意义。核心问题是由于临床特征重叠和常规检测有限,导致成人 CAP 中 RSV 诊断不足。

64ddc0ef44b0c16bc035da260ffc30d2f61a97c9.text: 该综述综合了韩国和国际数据,强调通过多样本分子检测来改进 RSV 检测。它没有指定数据库、搜索日期或研究计数,但强调了分子测试和现实世界 疫苗 有效性数据的使用。

569edf56d4861c6da9682b78ab943d7699fc2297.text: RSV 是成人 CAP 的重要诱因,尤其是老年人和患有慢性心肺疾病的人。主要结论包括 RSV 与心血管并发症、严重院内结局和继发细菌感染的关联,以及 诊断 分子检测的价值。

090797a0998a4ebebaa8ec0e9ea9133c37cb8d8e.text: 该审查指出了由于与其他呼吸道感染的临床重叠和有限的常规检测而导致的诊断挑战。证据差距包括需要对免疫功能低下和高危人群进行持续的授权后评估,以优化 疫苗接种 策略。

518e91d0b4181e78d4231ae20ef8184ad012c13d.text: 优先事项包括在 RSV 循环期间开发可行的诊断途径、加强 监测 以获得具有临床意义的结果,以及针对高危人群针对 疫苗接种。需要进一步的研究来为下一代预防策略提供信息。

ebbc8ee724235f9346304c1096b059f2b0a53c33.text: COVID-19 后时代的 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗接种 与日本老年人医疗信息源之间的关联:JACSIS 2024 年横断面研究。

71efb9e9d99719a92e16872d3ff70c94be762461.text: 该综述研究了日本老年人对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗接种 的吸收与他们的医疗信息来源、RSV 疫苗接种 资格知识以及后 COVID-19 时代的 疫苗接种 病史之间的关联。

81e9423037da5fc8bf270737ebb017aba28255a0.text: 该综述报告了一项在日本 60 岁或以上成年人中进行的全国性横断面在线调查,分析了 RSV 疫苗接种 状态与医疗信息来源、有关 RSV 感染和 疫苗接种 的知识以及既往 疫苗接种 病史之间的关联。

3ba993a2542a0a6763a50aaabac97ef6a1a236cf.text: 该综述没有报告亚组间的异质性、区域差异或 RSV 疫苗接种 吸收或信息源有效性的长期趋势。

5a210e6a488e229ac6a2aa15b5cca8682bbe17e1.text: 来自医疗保健专业人员的建议可能支持个性化的 RSV 疫苗接种 推广,特别是在有 疫苗接种 病史的个人中,而 LINE 等基于推送的信息渠道可能有助于在人群层面传播 RSV 相关知识。

ba417cb6e9b5fc851efeabdd482697551ceefa02.text: 二价 呼吸道合胞病毒 Prefusion F 疫苗 对于荷兰老年人的成本效益。

bf11e063446d492357ee55f9ed311b96482360a4.text: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV-LRTD) 引起的下呼吸道疾病给老年人和患有慢性病的成年人带来巨大的临床和经济负担。我们评估了实施该策略的成本效益。

a301693b6cdd4bf8900eda292d4cb944826cde71.text: 我们开发了一个静态 队列研究 模型,以证明荷兰成年人使用(与不使用)RSVpreF 时与 RSV-LRTD 相关的终生临床和经济结果(价格:180 欧元;特定年龄/风险的使用率:44.6-80.4%)。

f6cb08cc736269c5edbeac8e52411b2279156ff8.text: 模型输入包括人口特征、发病率[住院 (RSV-H)、全科医生就诊 (RSV-GP)、非医疗就诊 (RSV-NMA)]、死亡率、疫苗 有效性(基于真实世界和临床试验数据)、公用事业/公用事业、医疗保健成本、与发病率和 死亡率 相关的生产力损失相关的间接成本以及 疫苗 成本。折扣适用于成本(3%)和收益(1.5%)。

7bb68aa65815872e0bfd3f4576e8c9fa9b03eac6.text: 研究结果表明,RSVpreF 将大大减轻荷兰老年人 RSV 的临床和经济负担。因此,RSVpreF 将在该人群的余生中避免 16% 的住院治疗、15% 的死亡、16% 的医疗费用以及 20% 与 RSV 相关的间接费用。

aacbd479d8d53aeb76851f6cf0a6aa0ac5fb1c19.text: 基于二价 RSV 预融合 F 蛋白的 疫苗 (RSVpreF) 已被授权在荷兰所有年龄 ≥ 60 岁的成年人中使用,荷兰卫生委员会已推荐 RSV 疫苗接种 用于年龄 60-74 岁的高危人群和所有年龄 ≥ 75 岁的人群。

8475b39c5af484856f9d5472348bfacbf1595ee1.text: 在将可变性应用于关键输入的概率敏感性分析中,所有 1000 次重复均产生了卫生委员会支付意愿阈值内的成本效益比(< 50,000 欧元/获得的 QALY)。

721e3053a5f2f885e995991e2c68e0bb191324da.text: 帕利珠单抗用于卡塔尔高危人群的 呼吸道合胞病毒 免疫预防:呼吁采取行动。

7066d413731372c147ecc415ed8d714de376a202.text: 简介:早产儿和高危婴儿发生严重 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染的风险增加,导致住院时间延长、入住重症监护病房、呼吸支持和死亡。尽管 RSV 预防是卡塔尔的一项主要卫生优先事项,但目前缺乏 RSV 预防的国家指南。涵盖领域:本专家意见总结了卡塔尔和海湾合作委员会 (GCC) 的 RSV 负担以及当前的免疫预防实践和帕利珠单抗对高危婴儿有效性的现实证据。卡塔尔和海湾合作委员会相关专家的见解补充了文献综述的证据,以解决 RSV 预防方面的数据差距和异质性。综合研究结果支持针对具体情况的建议。专家意见:由 16 名专家组成的指导委员会于 2024 年 12 月召开,审查现有证据并讨论高危婴儿 RSV 预防的挑战。专家们查阅了文献并就建议达成了共识。帕利珠单抗得到既定有效性和长期安全性数据的支持,仍然是早产儿和高危儿科人群 RSV 预防的基石。它还承认有必要与其他海湾合作委员会国家合作并制定区域协议,以进一步加强 RSV 预防工作。

d94c40c1b32c99e42aaf3f172540f3347e932fd5.text: 本综述重点关注早产儿和高危婴儿的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染,检查卡塔尔和海湾合作委员会 (GCC) 的 RSV 负担,并评估当前的免疫预防实践和帕利珠单抗有效性的真实世界证据。

f3fe0e220dbc29d331346c53377974ae2490d1d8.text: 证据基础包括文献综述,并辅以 2024 年 12 月召开的由 16 名专家组成的指导委员会的专家见解,以解决 RSV 预防中的数据差距和异质性。

541d4277d97e1a391fed4bfc6a322e852696b23d.text: 帕利珠单抗被确立为早产儿和高危儿科人群 RSV 预防的基石,并得到有效性证据和长期安全性数据的支持。

4dbf2b4ffcc1ae87ca7b2582a8aebb53f3c05618.text: 通过补充文献综述以及与卡塔尔和海湾合作委员会相关的专家见解,解决了 RSV 预防的证据差距和异质性。

cbf63bda28ac8bdf38cdb11007629d3d597ea85c.text: 制定了针对具体情况的建议,强调需要与其他海湾合作委员会国家合作,制定区域协议并加强 RSV 预防工作。

1d6cf6ccaab14b4eb7c714e5ec36c52e03f9bd9b.text: 儿科医生对 呼吸道合胞病毒 以及当前和新兴预防策略的认知、知识和态度:来自土耳其一家三级护理医院的横断面调查研究

40609265eeac0243b5ae309ed831331689e3f70d.text: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染是五岁以下儿童下呼吸道感染的最常见原因,也是导致住院的重要因素。本研究旨在调查儿科医生(包括儿科专家和儿科住院医生)对 RSV 感染以及当地可用的(帕利珠单抗)和新出现的全球预防方案(尼塞韦单抗 和孕产妇 疫苗接种)的知识、意识和态度。对于这项横断面调查研究,数据是通过 2024 年 6 月至 2024 年 10 月期间对 216 名儿科医生(包括 76 名儿科专家和 140 名儿科住院医生)进行的在线调查收集的。几乎所有参与者 (97.7%) 都意识到应对高危人群的儿童进行 RSV 预防,以减少 RSV 感染对住院、发病率和 死亡率 的影响。然而,只有 78.7% 的参与者了解 疫苗接种 和用于预防 RSV 的单克隆抗体 (mAb)。共有 165 名 (76.4%) 参与者建议专门针对高危婴儿进行预防。还评估了对母亲 疫苗接种 的认识。相比之下,那些没有接种疫苗的人大多不知道这种疾病的发生频率和成本,并认为仅母乳就足以预防这种疾病。大约 55% 的儿科医生认为 RSV 预防措施没有得到有效实施。大约 83% 的参与者表示,如果他们有孩子,他们会选择 RSV 预防,并相信 RSV 预防可以有效影响许多人,从而减轻感染负担。共有 113 名参与者 (52.3%) 认为单克隆抗体应该给所有婴儿注射。值得注意的是,儿科专家对预防方法的认识明显高于儿科住院医生 (p = 0.004),而且临床症状和 传播 途径也存在差异。我们的研究结果表明,提高儿科医生对 RSV 诊断、治疗 和预防的了解对于优化预防策略至关重要。

9486406bca036924899ad094a4a86f9b56ef4e53.text: 本研究重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染(五岁以下儿童下呼吸道感染的最常见原因),并调查儿科医生对 RSV 预防的知识、意识和态度,包括当地可用的和新兴的选择。

2e3f1f6e189effb4a35d31bd36362db7e52efd4c.text: 这是一项横断面调查研究,通过 2024 年 6 月至 2024 年 10 月期间对 216 名儿科医生(76 名专家和 140 名住院医生)进行的在线调查进行。

d259b9e3d4c85888545a37ed989e717441c7523f.text: 几乎所有参与者 (97.7%) 都同意应对高危婴儿进行 RSV 预防,以减少住院、发病率和 死亡率。儿科专家对预防方法的认识明显高于住院医师 (p = 0.004)。

62c4fbdbca86e07d63b3488b62b384f9820d7a2b.text: 只有 78.7% 的参与者了解 疫苗接种 和用于预防 RSV 的单克隆抗体。大约 55% 的人认为预防措施没有得到有效实施,未接种疫苗的参与者往往不知道疾病的发生频率和费用。

327bba85288724f0d7e7a3d80104f857c9a4a4fd.text: 提高儿科医生对 RSV 诊断、治疗 和预防的了解对于优化预防策略至关重要。未来的研究应该解决意识差距和实施障碍。

42249d133d2a13bffc0326e20164cd0879e4f542.text: 英国孕妇和婴幼儿母亲对 疫苗 母亲的 疫苗 看法:一项定性研究。

f10f87f8d45019b7cccc209423ac3755b06b9af7.text: 背景:自 2024 年 9 月起,呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗接种 已在英国可供孕妇(妊娠 28 周起)使用。目的:探讨英国孕妇和婴幼儿母亲对 RSV 的了解和认识、RSV 疫苗接种 的认知和接受度以及对孕产妇 疫苗 分娩和沟通的偏好。方法:2024 年 7 月至 11 月期间,对 30 名母亲(最小的孩子不到 2 岁)进行了半结构化定性访谈,其中两名母亲怀有第二个孩子。这项研究是英国健康安全局对英格兰孕妇和产后妇女对 RSV 疫苗接种 态度的调查的后续研究。研究结果:虽然大多数母亲都听说过 RSV,但具有健康角色经验的母亲更有可能了解婴儿 RSV 的潜在严重性。据报道,母亲接受 RSV 的可能性很高,大多数母亲认为 RSV 疫苗接种 有利于保护婴儿。大多数母亲更喜欢采用混合方式进行 疫苗 沟通,包括在线获取信息(例如通过 NHS 网站)、书面来源(例如 NHS 制作的传单)以及通过与助产士交谈。为了方便起见,大多数母亲更愿意选择将 疫苗接种 纳入产前助产预约时间表,而不是去全科诊所单独预约。结论:为了支持母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 的决策和获取,女性在怀孕早期需要 疫苗 信息;通过一系列不同来源(即在线、纸质、面对面)提供信息;和 疫苗接种 在方便的地点分娩(即作为产前预约的一部分)。

1a0ef442371e612986d1efca8f1c0cdaf2c658ee.text: 旨在探索英国孕妇和婴幼儿母亲对 RSV 的了解和认识、RSV 疫苗接种 的认知和接受度以及对孕产妇 疫苗 分娩和沟通的偏好。

5192f049b71db4bc0169d3aadfce4e692ffc7082.text: 2024 年 7 月至 11 月期间,对 30 名母亲(最小的 2 岁以下孩子)进行了半结构化定性访谈,其中两名母亲怀有第二个孩子。

6a0a5911cb2c06d4fa51b36d69daefcb597c145f.text: 这项研究是英国健康安全局对英格兰孕妇和产后妇女对 RSV 疫苗接种 态度的调查的后续研究。

1eda853efbdf672bf43aa8276c6683d523b506c8.text: 尽管大多数母亲都听说过 RSV,但具有保健经验的母亲更有可能了解婴儿 RSV 的潜在严重性。据报道,母亲接受 RSV 的可能性很高,大多数母亲认为 RSV 疫苗接种 有利于保护婴儿。大多数母亲更喜欢采用混合方式进行 疫苗 沟通,包括通过在线、书面来源以及与助产士交谈获取信息。为了方便起见,大多数母亲更愿意选择将 疫苗接种 纳入产前助产预约时间表,而不是去全科诊所单独预约。

d9adee62a9c88089e7a8f6ee0c9da24cc82c175f.text: 为了支持母亲 RSV 疫苗接种 决策和获取,妇女在怀孕早期需要 疫苗 信息;通过一系列不同来源(即在线、纸质、面对面)提供信息;和 疫苗接种 在方便的地点分娩(即作为产前预约的一部分)。

0f9635d336c2a8523049a4230219fbe0f5fbec2e.text: 研究结果为通过解决沟通偏好和分娩便利性来提高母亲 RSV 疫苗 吸收的策略提供了信息,这可以加强公共卫生工作,保护婴儿免受 RSV 感染。

24e29993fadb292c2fc3e2cb9f4b6cd28caf97e0.text: 这项研究是定性的,并且基于一小部分母亲样本,限制了普遍性。然而,证据强度适中,因为该研究提供了与公共卫生目标一致的看法和偏好的详细见解。

2c83cc927281ef32ef123617b89d549f59e2ea4b.text: 泰国 呼吸道合胞病毒 大流行后的复苏:分子 流行病学 和儿童亚系更替,2023-2025 年。

116320fc05856e4d71d409438d6b92c7c394ac12.text: 摘要:在 COVID-19 大流行期间实施的非药物干预措施严重扰乱了全球 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的既定季节性。然而,大流行后时期热带地区 RSV 卷土重来和遗传多样性的分子流行病学数据仍然很少。本研究调查了 2023 年至 2025 年间泰国患有呼吸道疾病的儿童中传播的 RSV 的分子 流行病学、季节性趋势、遗传多样性和进化动态。在 5198 份呼吸道标本中,697 份 (13.4%) RSV 检测呈阳性,并在 2023 年观察到大流行后明显卷土重来 (18.3%)。RSV 季节性恢复到大流行前的典型模式,在雨季(7 月至 11 月)达到顶峰。观察到年龄分布的变化,其中 3 岁儿童负担最高(27.0%)。亚组优势交替明显,2023 年 (44.4%) 和 2025 年 (43.9%) 以 RSV-B 为主,2024 年以 RSV-A (46.3%) 为主。所有 RSV-A 菌株均属于 ON1 基因型(A.D 谱系),显示出优势亚谱系从 A.D.5.2 到 A.D.1.4 和 A.D.3 的连续年度更替。相反,RSV-B 菌株属于 BA9 基因型(B.D 谱系),B.D.E.1 亚谱系持续占优势(76.7%)。不同的谱系特异性氨基酸取代表明持续的病毒多样化和免疫选择压力。这些发现强调了持续分子 监测 为 RSV 预防策略提供信息的重要性。

0a51024aca5d372ff699360ffd6d0e5ab289d96d.text: 该研究旨在调查大流行后泰国 RSV 的分子 流行病学、季节趋势、遗传多样性和进化动态,因为 COVID-19 大流行期间的非药物干预措施扰乱了其在全球范围内既定的季节性。

e7e876a2561e221b18193c6921f6d24c78bedb4e.text: 这项研究分析了 2023 年至 2025 年间从患有呼吸道疾病的泰国儿童身上采集的呼吸道样本,其中 697 名(13.4%)RSV 检测呈阳性,显示出 2023 年疫情后明显复苏。

6a0c9c6ed25424bed7e5a2bbdc33f489943d8b7a.text: 该研究涉及检测呼吸道样本中 RSV,通过分子分析识别亚系,并跟踪三年来的季节性趋势和遗传多样性。

faba9576956cd368d50e243edabdb8354be0c33b.text: RSV 季节性恢复到大流行前的典型模式,在雨季(7 月至 11 月)达到顶峰。年龄分布发生变化,3 岁儿童的负担最高(27.0%)。亚组优势交替明显,2023 年 (44.4%) 和 2025 年 (43.9%) 以 RSV-B 为主,2024 年以 RSV-A (46.3%) 为主。

ee965bdee12d819814de34717d6f68ddcd50f7f3.text: 研究结果强调了RSV大流行后的复苏和亚谱系主导地位的变化,表明病毒持续多样化和免疫选择压力。

ea7cf9ca85b734c65437c288c22a8cb892f95acc.text: 这些结果强调需要持续的分子 监测 来更好地了解 RSV 动态并为热带地区的有针对性的预防策略提供信息。

8ecb81be9e6bc07904f486da262d3f0c0cd9116e.text: 该研究的局限性在于其重点关注泰国儿童,这可能会影响普遍性,并且依赖分子数据而没有临床结果评估,导致对亚谱系优势和多样化的解释信心不足。

644852e7feef56dbff2db08c7a6da0f0d9158234.text: 白藜芦醇抑制呼吸道合胞病毒核心靶基因筛选及机制分析

77b551033dfb38d3fcd56b253059e8251caa125f.text: 背景:呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是一种单链负义RNA病毒,是急性呼吸道感染的主要病原体,对婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下者的健康构成严重威胁。虽然已批准用于老年人的 疫苗 和用于婴儿的单克隆抗体预防,但有效的治疗药物仍然稀缺。白藜芦醇是一种天然存在于葡萄、浆果和其他食物中的酚类化合物,已被证实具有抗RSV活性,但其作用的分子机制仍不清楚。目的:本研究旨在利用计算生物学方法筛选白藜芦醇抗RSV的核心靶点和关键信号通路,提出可检验的研究假设,并为后续实验验证提供理论基础。方法:从数据库中总共检索到 261 个白藜芦醇相关靶标和 1196 个 RSV 相关靶标。使用Venny 2.1.0识别出67个重叠靶点,然后通过STRING/Cytoscape进行蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用(PPI)网络构建和拓扑分析以筛选核心靶点。使用DAVID数据库进行GO/KEGG富集分析,并使用PyMOL/AutoDock进行分子对接验证。结果:确定了 EGFR、SRC、HSP90AA1 和 ALB 等 10 个核心靶点。GO富集主要集中在PI3K-Akt信号转导、MAPK级联调控等生物过程,而KEGG通路则富集Ras信号通路等。分子对接显示白藜芦醇与核心靶标稳定结合,所有结合能<-5 kcal/mol。结论:这项计算机模拟研究预测,白藜芦醇可能通过靶向 宿主 蛋白(如 EGFR 和 SRC)并调节关键通路(包括 PI3K-Akt 和 Ras)来发挥抗 RSV 作用,补充了其与病毒蛋白直接相互作用的现有证据。该研究为抗RSV药物开发提供了新的见解,并为后续实验验证提供了理论基础。

b51bc6f24cb5cc65aa5faf2e4c0e028d52fdd13a.text: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是一种单链负义RNA病毒,是急性呼吸道感染的主要病原体,对婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下者的健康构成严重威胁。虽然已批准用于老年人的 疫苗 和用于婴儿的单克隆抗体预防,但有效的治疗药物仍然稀缺。

cd3beea8fd71da0bff8bd13ed52f98993a7233e2.text: 这项研究为抗RSV药物的开发提供了理论基础,并强调了未来实验研究中可以探索的潜在分子机制。

f478964a761ef56875d28f6325142acb843e8f76.text: 该研究基于计算机方法,可能无法完全捕捉生物相互作用的复杂性。然而,这些发现得到了计算分析和分子对接验证的支持,提供了中等程度的置信度。

f40c899f4d032a46e45290b4f9f77e3960694071.text: 与幼儿呼吸道病原体相关的症状:2019-2025 年。

6771c4d1f1a1aae95570666375690667a4917a8e.text: 背景和目标:急性呼吸道疾病(ARI)在生命早期很常见,会引起一系列呼吸道症状。我们描述了呼吸道感染发作的症状特征和医疗结果。方法:从 2019 年 11 月至 2025 年 8 月,对俄亥俄州辛辛那提健康美国婴儿和儿童的纵向出生 队列研究 进行每周中鼻甲鼻拭子采集和每两周一次的症状调查。在 Luminex NxTAG 呼吸道病原体面板和 Flu SC2 检测中对鼻拭子进行病原体靶标检测。病原体特异性感染与时间相应的症状调查相关。去除共感染以仅观察独立的病原体症状。结果:我们从 1223 名独特儿童中捕获了 15 898 个 ARI。与年龄较大的儿童相比,婴儿更容易因甲型流感(比值比 [OR] = 4.73)、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) A (OR = 2.52)、RSV B (OR = 2.22)、人类偏肺病毒 (OR = 2.36) 和 SARS-CoV-2 (OR = 3.99) 出现呼吸窘迫/呼吸困难(所有 P < 0.01)但不是乙型流感(P = 0.36)或副流感(P = 0.10)。医院和急诊科的医疗护理也有类似的相关性。与乙型流感相比,甲型流感出现发烧(OR = 2.77,P = 0.01)和厌食(OR = 2.94,P = 0.01)的几率更大。无症状感染很常见。超过四分之三的症状发作是在家治疗的。四分之一的 RSV 感染和三分之一的流感感染发作期间发生呕吐和/或腹泻。结论:我们的结果强调了美国 队列研究 健康儿童呼吸道感染症状和结果的显着差异。了解为什么一些幼儿会出现严重症状,而另一些则相对未受影响,可以为改善儿童健康提供可行的机会。此外,我们观察到呼吸道感染期间频繁腹泻和/或呕吐,以及甲型和乙型流感症状之间的细微差别。

abd858411dcd7c1d1419f03117c9f487b07a1bcd.text: 背景和目标:急性呼吸道疾病(ARI)在生命早期很常见,会引起一系列呼吸道症状。

599e6d366db480747e99f53e868679fb6164420f.text: 我们描述了呼吸道感染发作的症状特征和医疗结果。从 2019 年 11 月至 2025 年 8 月,从俄亥俄州辛辛那提健康美国婴儿和儿童的纵向出生 队列研究 中收集每周中鼻甲鼻拭子和每两周一次的症状调查。

af9bde8673a421dedf4cc76370c97c3d876f3382.text: 在 Luminex NxTAG 呼吸道病原体面板和 Flu SC2 检测中对鼻拭子进行病原体靶标检测。病原体特异性感染与时间相应的症状调查相关。去除共感染以仅观察独立的病原体症状。

8282b795a5a948074875c42935b3035426736cb8.text: 我们从 1223 名独特儿童中捕获了 15 898 个 ARI。与年龄较大的儿童相比,使用 呼吸道合胞病毒 A (OR = 2.52) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 B (OR = 2.22) 的婴儿更容易出现呼吸窘迫/呼吸困难(均 P < 0.01)。四分之一的 RSV 感染发作期间发生呕吐和/或腹泻。

5522d24ed512da7c7d9c650a61460b8849961821.text: 我们的结果强调了美国 队列研究 健康儿童呼吸道感染症状和结果的显着差异。了解为什么一些幼儿会出现严重症状,而另一些则相对未受影响,可以为改善儿童健康提供可行的机会。

2b85c63a79d60dfb461b4371322517ccc4e639ba.text: 研究结果为 监测 和幼儿 RSV 感染的临床管理提供了信息,强调需要有针对性的干预措施和了解症状变异性以改善结果。

01cb2f272161a46f451884178a233f43f81de842.text: 该研究是在单一美国 队列研究 中进行的,可能限制了普遍性。由于样本量大和纵向设计,证据强度很高。

dc454d762c4b42505802d797ae570f646fc15ed2.text: MATISSE(安全性和功效母体免疫研究)母体 呼吸道合胞病毒 预融合 F 蛋白 疫苗 试验的功效、安全性和免疫原性:修正。

a528080795e9b3f4c712b90af42ad1df583626b4.text: 该研究旨在评估母体 RSV 预融合 F 蛋白 疫苗 预防婴儿 RSV 感染的有效性、安全性和免疫原性。

0ad1b99128a751a7b2fb483ce37f2a88c7ec46c4.text: 这是一项在不同国家的多个中心进行的随机、双盲、安慰剂对照试验,受试者为在妊娠晚期接受 疫苗 或安慰剂的孕妇。

09694cfede6acf185a0007b0b5bced81ee0ff31a.text: 在妊娠晚期对参与者进行 疫苗 治疗,并在 疫苗接种 治疗后对婴儿进行 180 天的随访,以评估 RSV 感染和 毛细支气管炎 等结果。

52298e43aca15ecd9f1c5b643ce4f4c41fc793a3.text: 疫苗 在 180 天内对全因医疗下呼吸道疾病的疗效为 4.1%(95% CI,-9.5 至 16.0),且没有重大安全问题报告。

19828a6b98bffcfdac38e2453c54df9a09ae448b.text: 作者将结果解释为表明 疫苗 对婴儿 RSV 相关下呼吸道疾病具有适度的保护作用,这是孕产妇免疫策略中的一个新发现。

28b3cd5214e4640ecf27327afb82a049a44aec1e.text: 这些发现表明,具有预输注 F 蛋白 疫苗 的母体 疫苗接种 可能为减少婴儿 RSV 相关疾病提供潜在策略,支持该领域的进一步研究和开发。

f90125c9ca99dd3eccfed213df729170072ac86f.text: 由于研究的特定人群和地理区域,该研究的样本量相对较小,普遍性有限,但由于严格的设计和更正的疗效时间范围,证据被认为是中等的。
